modules.purpose: Convert between spreadsheet cell addresses and zero-based row/column indices, and format numeric indices back to canonical addresses.
exports: columnToIndex(column: string): number — throws Error for an empty or invalid column label
indexToColumn(index: number): string — throws Error for a negative or non-integer index
parseAddress(address: string): {row: number, column: number} — throws Error for malformed addresses
formatAddress(row: number, column: number): string — throws Error for negative or non-integer indices

modules.purpose: Parse formula source into an abstract syntax tree for arithmetic expressions, cell references, ranges, and supported aggregate functions.
exports: parseFormula(source: string): Node — throws Error when source is not a formula or contains an unknown token, unsupported function, malformed reference/range, or invalid syntax

Node: object — AST node shapes are {type:"number",value:number}, {type:"cell",row:number,column:number}, {type:"range",start:{row:number,column:number},end:{row:number,column:number}}, {type:"unary",op:"+"|"-",operand:Node}, {type:"binary",op:"+"|"-"|"*"|"/",left:Node,right:Node}, or {type:"call",name:"SUM"|"AVG"|"MIN"|"MAX",range:Node}
acceptance: parseFormula("=1+2*3") produces a binary multiplication whose right operand is number 6
parseFormula("=A1") produces a cell node for row 0, column 0
parseFormula("=SUM(A1:B3)") produces a SUM call with a range node

modules.purpose: Evaluate parsed formulas against a sheet, including dependency values, range aggregates, empty-cell coercion, and arithmetic error propagation.
exports: evaluateFormula(node: Node, context: {getCell: (row: number, column: number) => unknown, getRange: (start: {row: number, column: number}, end: {row: number, column: number}) => unknown[]}): number|string — returns #DIV/0 for division by zero, propagates existing #CYCLE and #DIV/0 values, and treats empty cells as 0

evaluateRange(node: Node, context: {getCell: (row: number, column: number) => unknown, getRange: (start: {row: number, column: number}, end: {row: number, column: number}) => unknown[]}): unknown[] — returns the expanded values of a range node

modules.purpose: Encode and decode spreadsheet data as CSV, preserving raw cell contents including formula strings.
exports: toCsv(rows: Array<Array<string|number>>): string — throws Error for ragged rows or non-supported values
fromCsv(src: string): string[][] — parses quoted fields, escaped quotes, embedded commas/newlines, and CRLF or LF line endings; throws Error for malformed quoting

modules.purpose: Provide the in-memory spreadsheet API, dependency tracking, topological recalculation, cycle detection, computed values, and CSV import/export.
exports: class Spreadsheet — constructor() creates an empty sheet; setCell(address: string, rawValue: string|number): void — stores raw input, recalculates dependents, and marks every cell in a cycle as "#CYCLE"; getCell(address: string): string|number — returns the raw formula or computed constant value; getComputedValue(address: string): string|number — returns the computed value, treating an empty cell as 0; getRawValue(address: string): string|number|undefined — returns raw input without calculation; getDependencies(address: string): string[] — returns direct precedent addresses in source order; toCsv(): string — exports rows 1..maxRow and columns A..maxCol using computed values, with formulas exported as computed values; fromCsv(src: string): void — replaces the sheet contents with raw CSV fields, treating each field as a number when finite and numeric, otherwise as a string; recalculate(): void — recomputes all formula cells in dependency order and assigns "#CYCLE" to every cell participating in a circular dependency
acceptance: A sheet with A1=1, B1="=A1+1", C1="=B1*2" has computed values 1, 2, and 4
Changing A1 to 5 updates B1 to 6 and C1 to 12
Setting A1="=B1" and B1="=A1" makes both computed values "#CYCLE" without throwing
A formula referencing an empty cell treats it as 0, and "=A1/0" computes "#DIV/0"
A sheet containing A1="hello" and B1=2 exports CSV with "hello,2"
Importing CSV containing "=A1+1" preserves the raw formula in getRawValue("A1")
